thread:
sanjay: pushed an experiment to switch the paged-KV allocator to a segmap+arena mode on the paged-attn branch. curious about fragmentation/throughput impact. noticed a ~12% p99 tail increase on a few FlashAttention variants. logs + simple perf output below. anybody seen this pattern before?

maya: thanks for flagging. do we have a small repro that hits the hotpath (long-context, many concurrent streams)? can you paste the perf stat and the kernel chosen?

sanjay: repro is here: run microbench with --seq-len=2048 --concurrency=24 --batching=auto and model=redwood-v1-paged (patched). quick stats:
```
throughput (tokens/s):  1.0x baseline -> 0.88x with segmap
p50 latency:  +3%
p95 latency:  +9%
p99 latency:  +12%
cpu/gpu-util: same
alloc churn: +32% (small pages)
kv-page-alloc-fails: 0
```
kernel selection trace: FlashAttn-v2 fallback -> FlashAttn-fused on cold path; stays fused during steady-state.

lucy: fwiw, segmap defers coalescing and prefers smaller pages to avoid long pauses. could be increasing cache churn so the attention kernel sees more KV page misses which then flips the kernel selection heuristic into a higher-latency kernel. are you seeing more KV cache evictions?

sanjay: yes, alloc telemetry shows higher freelist fragmentation and more frequent page reclamation (short bursts). attaching snippet from allocator counters: `free_runs=480, coalesce_ops=22, split_ops=270, avg_frag_pct=18`. baseline had avg_frag_pct=6.

tj: this smells like an interplay between batching heuristic and prefix/KV cache locality. If batching grows batch size because latency appeared stable early, the KV pager then hits more unique keys and forces more page churn. Could we try forcing batching=min or disable auto-batching for the run?

sanjay: did a quick run with --batching=min: p99 back to +4% (better) and throughput 0.95x. So batching is amplifying the effect.

maya: good datapoint. Two axes to explore: change allocator (grow arena size, increase coalesce aggressiveness) OR make batching heuristic more fragile to eviction signals (reduce growth factor when page-evict-rate > X).

lucy: i can prototype a coalesce-after-threshold tweak: if free_runs > 200 && split_ops > 100 then run background coalesce more aggressively. might smooth fragmentation without making pages huge.

sanjay: also thinking kernel-selection heuristic should look at recent KV page fault rate and prefer the kernel variant that tolerates smaller KV locality (the fused path seems sensitive). we should add a telemetry signal: kv_page_fault_rate_1m to kernel selector.

ops-bot: benchmark queued: paged-attn/segmap-arena/1769128888/step1 (runs scheduled on ci-gpu-14).

bench-bot: quick micro results (after disabling auto-batching):
```
variant: segmap+arena, batching=auto -> throughput 0.88x, p99 +12%
variant: segmap+arena, batching=min  -> throughput 0.95x, p99 +4%
variant: baseline-heap, batching=auto-> throughput 1.00x, p99 baseline
```

tj: ok plan: (1) lucy prototypes coalesce tweak, (2) sanjay adds kv_page_fault_rate to kernel selector, (3) maya runs matrix with batching growth factors (0.5/0.75/1.0) and allocator flags. can we keep each experiment scoped so we can attribute wins?

lucy: will start today. i'll also add a small probe that emits `kv_page_fault_rate_30s` to logs so we can correlate with kernel switches.

sanjay: i'll wire the selector metric and a guard that keeps kernel pinned for 5s after a switch if page-fault-rate > threshold (simple debounce).

maya: great. put PRs against paged-attn-experiments branch and tag me. try to keep individual changes small. thanks! :thumbsup:

tj: adding that to the perf board; flagging as medium priority since this impacts p99 for long-context clients.

lucy: FYI i'll also run a synthetic that intentionally fragments the KV space (random free/alloc churn) to stress the coalesce. will report numbers here.

sanjay: thanks all — will follow up with links to PRs and CI runs when ready.
